justice noun

fairness, giving each their due

also fairness, equity, righteousness, just, injustice, justly, fairly

classical

Cic. Off. 1.20: jūstitiae prīmum mūnus est ut nē cui quis noceat nisi lacessītus injūriā
Traupman 155, 195
Traupman 195
Traupman 336

jūstitia, jūstitiae f.

noun, first declension

Justice as a virtue: cōnstāns et perpetua voluntās jūs suum cuique tribuendī (Just. Inst. 1.1.1, Lewis & Short). In the Vulgate also righteousness. Injustice is injūstitia (Traupman 154). The courts and the law are jūdicia and jūs (see court, law).

Other words

  • aequitās, aequitātis f. — fairness, equity

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.240: prō aequitāte contrā jūs dīcere (Lewis & Short); Traupman 152; Traupman 312

    Fair dealing, which looks to goodwill where jūstitia gives only what is strictly due, so that one can plead it against the letter of the law; sometimes simply justice. Its first sense is evenness, and aequitās animī is calm of mind (Lewis & Short).

  • injūstitia, injūstitiae f. — injustice

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.23 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 154

  • jūstus, jūsta, jūstum — just, fair

    also used · classical · Traupman 335

  • jūstē — justly, fairly

    adverb · also used · classical · Traupman 336

Examples

  • jūstitiae prīmum mūnus est ut nē cui quis noceat nisi lacessītus injūriā

    the first duty of justice is that no one should harm anyone unless provoked by a wrongCic. Off. 1.20

  • fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs, id est dictōrum conventōrumque cōnstantia et vēritās

    and the foundation of justice is good faith: keeping to what has been said and agreed, and truth in itCic. Off. 1.23

  • ut forīs ita domī, ut in magnīs ita in parvīs, ut in aliēnīs ita in suīs agitāre jūstitiam

    to practise justice at home as abroad, in small things as in great, with one’s own as with others’Plin. Ep. 8.2.2

  • remōtā itaque jūstitiā quid sunt rēgna nisi magna latrōcinia?

    take away justice, then, and what are kingdoms but robbery on a grand scale?Aug. Civ. 4.4

See also law, court.
